# dsh-ollama-web
English | 日本語 | 中文
Ollama Cloud web search and optional web fetch provider for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), with a Web UI se
ttings card. One npm package provides both the host backend and the browser card. Search uses Ollama
; `web_fetch` stays on DSH's built-in HTTP provider unless you explicitly enable the optional Ollama
ays on DSH's built-in HTTP provider unless you explicitly enable the optional Ollama fetch provider.

- Search endpoint defaults to `https://ollama.com/api/web_search`
- Optional fetch endpoint defaults

to `https://ollama.com/api/web_fetch`; off by default
- Configure the API key in the card (write-on

ly) or via `OLLAMA_API_KEY`
- Update checks, install, and opt-in auto-update are included
- Default
`web_fetch` remains the credential-free DSH HTTP provider
## Requirements

- DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 (peer `>=0.2.1-rc.1 <0.3.0`), tested on this version
- DSH 0.3.x is not supported y

et (planned for 3.0); see docs/COMPATIBILITY.md
- Node.js >= 20.3
- An Ollama Cloud API key from <ht
tps://ollama.com/settings/keys>
## Install
One package provides the `web_search` backend, the optional fetch provider and the settings card. In

e Web UI. npm: dsh-ollama-web

Open **Plugins -> `dsh-ollama-web` -> `ollama-web` -> Configure** and turn on
**Use Ollama for web s

earch**. The card writes `web.searchProvider` for you;
no profile patch is needed.

For a manual pin, add **both** fields to
`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`:

`fetchProvider: http` keeps `web_fetch` on DSH's built-in HTTP provider. A
`web` entry replaces the

whole row config, so keep both fields when you edit
it. The card shows which provider is currently e

ffective even when Ollama is
not selected.
### Optional Ollama fetch provider

To use Ollama for `web_fetch`, turn on **Use Ollama for web fetch** in the card.
The card writes `en

ableFetchProvider: true` and `web.fetchProvider: ollama`
together, so the provider is registered and
pinned in one save.
For a manual pin, both entries are required:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`web` replaces its whole config, so keep `searchProvider: ollama` when you
change `fetchProvider`. W

ith only `enableFetchProvider: true`, `web_fetch`
reports `WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS` when both the HTT

P and Ollama fetch providers
are usable. With only `fetchProvider: ollama`, it reports
`WEB_PROVIDER

_CONFIGURED_UNAVAILABLE` because the Ollama provider is disabled.
The settings card handles both fie

lds together; these warnings apply when you
edit the profile patch by hand.
Ollama does not expose the target page's HTTP status or final redirect URL. A successful Ollama fetc
h is reported to DSH as `HTTP 200` for the requested URL; title, main content and links are folded i
nto the text result. Keep `fetchProvider: http` when target status fidelity or DSH's local SSRF boun
result. Keep `fetchProvider: http` when target status fidelity or DSH's local SSRF boundary matters.
### Provider selection and the profile patch

- The card writes DSH's `web` settings namespace, not `cordis.patch.yml`. The
profile patch remains

the deployment default; remove an `- id: web` entry if
you want the card to own the selection.
- If

a profile patch pins `searchProvider: ollama`, the card shows the search
switch as pinned and disabl

ed. Remove that patch line to manage it from the
card. The fetch switch can still override a pinned

fetch provider with the
built-in HTTP provider.
- The built-in Web search settings page edits the sa

me `web` selection. Use one
surface at a time; a conflicting save is refused and the card keeps your

draft.
- `DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER` / `DSH_WEB_FETCH_PROVIDER` environment variables
override the sa

ved selection at runtime. The card cannot see those
environment variables, so its status reflects th
e saved `web` config.

## Security
- Host plugins run in-process, outside the workspace sandbox. Review plugins before installing and p

in versions.
- Search is HTTPS-only, refuses redirects, caps response/query/snippet sizes, and allow

s only `http(s)` result URLs.
- The optional fetch provider sends the requested URL to Ollama. Ollam
a performs the fetch, so this provider does not provide DSH HTTP's local DNS-pinning/SSRF boundary.
It rejects non-http(s) URLs, embedded credentials and obvious local/private destinations, but URLs a

re still disclosed to Ollama; do not use it for internal or secret-bearing URLs.
- No query, URL or

API key logging, no telemetry, no custom session events.
- Search and optional fetch contact only `o
llama.com` by default. Updates contact the npm registry (fallback: npmmirror) only on explicit actio
n, while auto-update is enabled, or when the update screen opens after five minutes without a succes
sful check, and send only the package name. Changing `baseURL` changes where the key, queries and fe

tch URLs go.
- Update tarballs are checked against the npm SHA-512 integrity; symlinks, traversal an

d oversized entries are rejected. No npm lifecycle script runs.
- On a successful self-update the up
dater may rewrite only the exact `dsh-ollama-web` dependency value in the profile `package.json`. It

does not run npm/pnpm and does not rewrite `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- Auto-update installs new code withou

t a prompt. It is opt-in and limited to the current major version.
- The client card makes no third-
party external request. It reads update state and performs update actions only through DSH's same-or

igin Connection RPC to the host. It does not use `innerHTML` / `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- Release

and self-review settings: docs/RELEASE-HARDENING.md.
- The published package carries npm provenance.
See docs/PROVENANCE.md and docs/SMOKE-RESULTS.md for verification records, and SECURITY.md / docs/S
ECURITY.md for the full policy.
